weekly_review.report:
Value-tier water-based strawberry ice bars are experiencing strong replenishment demand across all four sales districts, with store requests over the last 14 days reaching 15,785 units against an expectation of 10,913 units (a 44.6% positive deviation). Over the last 7 days, requested volume accelerated to 56.3% above baseline. Because of recent delivery delays across four supplier shipments, warehouse fulfillment declined to an 88.2% fill rate, leaving 1,859 store-requested units unfulfilled. The estimated sustained demand effect is +38.2%. In contrast, value-tier creamy strawberry bars remained virtually unchanged (-0.6% deviation from expectation), demonstrating that the surge is isolated to light, thirst-quenching water ice formats.

Simultaneously, store requests for chocolate-coated treats softened across the network, totaling 23,595 units against 25,030 expected units (-5.7% deviation over 14 days, widening to -8.6% over the last 7 days). The estimated sustained demand effect is -4.6%. Warehouse fulfillment for chocolate lines remains healthy at 99.3%, with 362 cases on open orders scheduled to arrive.

Cold-store occupancy is projected at 61.3 pallets under proposed adjustments, safely within the whole-warehouse physical limit of 62.0 pallets. Recommended purchasing actions increase value water-based strawberry lines by 134 cases to alleviate store stockouts and capture an estimated HK$12,793 in avoided lost margin, funded in space by reducing chocolate-coated commitments by 43 cases.

presentation.title: Value strawberry water ices surge while chocolate-coated lines soften
presentation.html:
Main observations

All districts · 4 SKUs

Value strawberry water ices

+38.2%
Recent 14d requests +44.6% vs forecast · 88.2% fill rate

Replenishment requests for refreshing value-tier strawberry bars have outpaced baseline expectations across all four districts, accelerating to 56.3% above forecast over the last 7 days. Inbound supplier delays on four receipts exacerbated distribution pressure, pulling warehouse fulfillment down to 88.2%.

All districts · 10 SKUs

Other chocolate-coated

-4.6%
Recent 14d requests -5.7% vs forecast · 99.3% fill rate

Store orders across chocolate-coated cones and bars softened across all territories, dropping to 8.6% below forecast during the most recent week. Service levels remain strong at 99.3% fill rate, but 362 cases are already in transit, risking unnecessary cold-store inventory accumulation.

Mid-summer replenishment is pivoting sharply toward thirst-quenching fruit water ices while richer chocolate confectionery demand moderates. Expanding water ice intake is essential to eliminate store shortages, with cold-store space readily freed by trimming incoming chocolate lines.

Secondary observations

All districts · 3 SKUs

Value strawberry creamy ice bars

-0.6%
Recent 14d requests: 6,345 vs 6,384 expected

Value dairy-based strawberry ice bars remain virtually flat against baseline forecasts. This stability confirms that recent surges reflect specific demand for water-based fruit bars rather than a general strawberry flavour trend across dairy lines.

Merchandising and planning checks

Please confirm whether any retail store promotions or outdoor marketing campaigns specifically targeted value water ices in mid-July, and check if supplier SUP08 can expedite the Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar batch to recover buffer stock.

metadata.inventory_provenance: Synthetic historical stock at the end of yesterday. Confirmed demo orders are recorded, not physically applied to this historical simulation.

review.report:
Value-tier water-based strawberry ice bars are experiencing strong replenishment demand across all four sales districts, with store requests over the last 14 days reaching 15,785 units against an expectation of 10,913 units (a 44.6% positive deviation). Over the last 7 days, requested volume accelerated to 56.3% above baseline. Because of recent delivery delays across four supplier shipments, warehouse fulfillment declined to an 88.2% fill rate, leaving 1,859 store-requested units unfulfilled. The estimated sustained demand effect is +38.2%. In contrast, value-tier creamy strawberry bars remained virtually unchanged (-0.6% deviation from expectation), demonstrating that the surge is isolated to light, thirst-quenching water ice formats.

Simultaneously, store requests for chocolate-coated treats softened across the network, totaling 23,595 units against 25,030 expected units (-5.7% deviation over 14 days, widening to -8.6% over the last 7 days). The estimated sustained demand effect is -4.6%. Warehouse fulfillment for chocolate lines remains healthy at 99.3%, with 362 cases on open orders scheduled to arrive.

Cold-store occupancy is projected at 61.3 pallets under proposed adjustments, safely within the whole-warehouse physical limit of 62.0 pallets. Recommended purchasing actions increase value water-based strawberry lines by 134 cases to alleviate store stockouts and capture an estimated HK$12,793 in avoided lost margin, funded in space by reducing chocolate-coated commitments by 43 cases.

presentation.title: Value strawberry water ices surge while chocolate-coated lines soften
presentation.html:
Main observations

All districts · 4 SKUs

Value strawberry water ices

+38.2%
Recent 14d requests +44.6% vs forecast · 88.2% fill rate

Replenishment requests for refreshing value-tier strawberry bars have outpaced baseline expectations across all four districts, accelerating to 56.3% above forecast over the last 7 days. Inbound supplier delays on four receipts exacerbated distribution pressure, pulling warehouse fulfillment down to 88.2%.

All districts · 10 SKUs

Other chocolate-coated

-4.6%
Recent 14d requests -5.7% vs forecast · 99.3% fill rate

Store orders across chocolate-coated cones and bars softened across all territories, dropping to 8.6% below forecast during the most recent week. Service levels remain strong at 99.3% fill rate, but 362 cases are already in transit, risking unnecessary cold-store inventory accumulation.

Mid-summer replenishment is pivoting sharply toward thirst-quenching fruit water ices while richer chocolate confectionery demand moderates. Expanding water ice intake is essential to eliminate store shortages, with cold-store space readily freed by trimming incoming chocolate lines.

Secondary observations

All districts · 3 SKUs

Value strawberry creamy ice bars

-0.6%
Recent 14d requests: 6,345 vs 6,384 expected

Value dairy-based strawberry ice bars remain virtually flat against baseline forecasts. This stability confirms that recent surges reflect specific demand for water-based fruit bars rather than a general strawberry flavour trend across dairy lines.

Merchandising and planning checks

Please confirm whether any retail store promotions or outdoor marketing campaigns specifically targeted value water ices in mid-July, and check if supplier SUP08 can expedite the Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar batch to recover buffer stock.

Action recommendations

claims.text: Store replenishment requests for value water-based strawberry ice bars reached 15,785 units over the past 14 days against an expected 10,913 units, representing a 44.6% positive deviation from baseline expectations.
The estimated sustained demand effect for value price water-based strawberry products is +38.2% with an 80% confidence interval of 35.1% to 41.3%.
Warehouse fulfillment for value water-based strawberry ice bars slipped to an 88.2% fill rate, leaving 1,859 requested units unfulfilled across 20 stores.
Suppliers experienced delivery delays on 4 of 8 recent shipments for value water-based strawberry items, while 153 cases remain on open purchase orders.
Chocolate-coated ice cream requests totaled 23,595 units over the last 14 days compared to an expectation of 25,030 units, a deviation of -5.7%, widening to -8.6% over the last 7 days.
The estimated sustained demand effect for other chocolate-coated items is -4.6% with an 80% confidence interval of -6.0% to -3.2%.
Warehouse fulfillment for chocolate-coated items remained healthy at a 99.3% fill rate with 362 cases already scheduled across 8 open inbound shipments.

Value creamy strawberry ice creams tracked expectations closely at 6,345 requested units versus 6,384 expected (-0.6% deviation), indicating demand uplift is confined to water-based fruit bars rather than all strawberry lines.
Total projected warehouse storage footprint across all proposed cohort adjustments sits at 61.3 pallets, safely within the warehouse physical limit of 62.0 pallets.

Sustained high summer temperatures appear to be driving store replenishment toward light, thirst-quenching water ice bars at the expense of richer confectionery formats, resulting in warehouse stock pressure.
Increase purchase orders for value water-based strawberry ice bars by 134 cases (+2.2 pallets) to protect store service levels and capture an estimated HK$12,793 in avoided lost margin.
Reduce purchase orders for chocolate-coated products by 43 cases (-0.8 pallets) to adjust to softening store demand and preserve warehouse cold-store capacity.

questions.text: Did retail marketing or store-level displays launch in mid-July specifically featuring water-based fruit ice bars?
Can supplier SUP08 confirm shipment reliability for Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar to help rebuild warehouse cover?

items.title: Are local retail stores planning summer displays or value promotions for water-based fruit bars over early August?
Should warehouse receiving schedule off-peak delivery windows to manage the 1.3-pallet inherited storage overhang?
Did regional stores report any localized end-cap displays or outdoor marketing initiatives driving the sharp replenishment surge in water-based strawberry bars?
Do merchandisers anticipate chocolate-coated demand stabilizing as school holidays progress, or should we plan for extended softness into August?

weekly_review.report:
Value-tier water-based strawberry ice bars are experiencing strong replenishment demand across all four sales districts, with store requests over the last 14 days reaching 15,785 units against an expectation of 10,913 units (a 44.6% positive deviation). Over the last 7 days, requested volume accelerated to 56.3% above baseline. Because of recent delivery delays across four supplier shipments, warehouse fulfillment declined to an 88.2% fill rate, leaving 1,859 store-requested units unfulfilled. The estimated sustained demand effect is +38.2%. In contrast, value-tier creamy strawberry bars remained virtually unchanged (-0.6% deviation from expectation), demonstrating that the surge is isolated to light, thirst-quenching water ice formats.

Simultaneously, store requests for chocolate-coated treats softened across the network, totaling 23,595 units against 25,030 expected units (-5.7% deviation over 14 days, widening to -8.6% over the last 7 days). The estimated sustained demand effect is -4.6%. Warehouse fulfillment for chocolate lines remains healthy at 99.3%, with 362 cases on open orders scheduled to arrive.

Cold-store occupancy is projected at 61.3 pallets under proposed adjustments, safely within the whole-warehouse physical limit of 62.0 pallets. Recommended purchasing actions increase value water-based strawberry lines by 134 cases to alleviate store stockouts and capture an estimated HK$12,793 in avoided lost margin, funded in space by reducing chocolate-coated commitments by 43 cases.

presentation.title: Value strawberry water ices surge while chocolate-coated lines soften
presentation.html:
Main observations

All districts · 4 SKUs

Value strawberry water ices

+38.2%
Recent 14d requests +44.6% vs forecast · 88.2% fill rate

Replenishment requests for refreshing value-tier strawberry bars have outpaced baseline expectations across all four districts, accelerating to 56.3% above forecast over the last 7 days. Inbound supplier delays on four receipts exacerbated distribution pressure, pulling warehouse fulfillment down to 88.2%.

All districts · 10 SKUs

Other chocolate-coated

-4.6%
Recent 14d requests -5.7% vs forecast · 99.3% fill rate

Store orders across chocolate-coated cones and bars softened across all territories, dropping to 8.6% below forecast during the most recent week. Service levels remain strong at 99.3% fill rate, but 362 cases are already in transit, risking unnecessary cold-store inventory accumulation.

Mid-summer replenishment is pivoting sharply toward thirst-quenching fruit water ices while richer chocolate confectionery demand moderates. Expanding water ice intake is essential to eliminate store shortages, with cold-store space readily freed by trimming incoming chocolate lines.

Secondary observations

All districts · 3 SKUs

Value strawberry creamy ice bars

-0.6%
Recent 14d requests: 6,345 vs 6,384 expected

Value dairy-based strawberry ice bars remain virtually flat against baseline forecasts. This stability confirms that recent surges reflect specific demand for water-based fruit bars rather than a general strawberry flavour trend across dairy lines.

Merchandising and planning checks

Please confirm whether any retail store promotions or outdoor marketing campaigns specifically targeted value water ices in mid-July, and check if supplier SUP08 can expedite the Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar batch to recover buffer stock.

Action recommendations

claims.text: Store replenishment requests for value water-based strawberry ice bars reached 15,785 units over the past 14 days against an expected 10,913 units, representing a 44.6% positive deviation from baseline expectations.
The estimated sustained demand effect for value price water-based strawberry products is +38.2% with an 80% confidence interval of 35.1% to 41.3%.
Warehouse fulfillment for value water-based strawberry ice bars slipped to an 88.2% fill rate, leaving 1,859 requested units unfulfilled across 20 stores.
Suppliers experienced delivery delays on 4 of 8 recent shipments for value water-based strawberry items, while 153 cases remain on open purchase orders.
Chocolate-coated ice cream requests totaled 23,595 units over the last 14 days compared to an expectation of 25,030 units, a deviation of -5.7%, widening to -8.6% over the last 7 days.
The estimated sustained demand effect for other chocolate-coated items is -4.6% with an 80% confidence interval of -6.0% to -3.2%.
Warehouse fulfillment for chocolate-coated items remained healthy at a 99.3% fill rate with 362 cases already scheduled across 8 open inbound shipments.

Value creamy strawberry ice creams tracked expectations closely at 6,345 requested units versus 6,384 expected (-0.6% deviation), indicating demand uplift is confined to water-based fruit bars rather than all strawberry lines.
Total projected warehouse storage footprint across all proposed cohort adjustments sits at 61.3 pallets, safely within the warehouse physical limit of 62.0 pallets.

Sustained high summer temperatures appear to be driving store replenishment toward light, thirst-quenching water ice bars at the expense of richer confectionery formats, resulting in warehouse stock pressure.
Increase purchase orders for value water-based strawberry ice bars by 134 cases (+2.2 pallets) to protect store service levels and capture an estimated HK$12,793 in avoided lost margin.
Reduce purchase orders for chocolate-coated products by 43 cases (-0.8 pallets) to adjust to softening store demand and preserve warehouse cold-store capacity.

cohort_cards.effect_basis: Estimated sustained change in requested/forecast ratio from baseline to recent, after shrinkage; not the raw recent requested-minus-forecast percentage.
cohort_cards.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.
cohort_cards.pallet_change_basis: Footprint of the change in total purchased cases; not a change in simultaneous warehouse peak occupancy.
cohort_cards.peak_capacity_scope: Whole warehouse with ALL cohort adjustments and current overrides already included together.

leaf.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.

trace.tree: inverse-variance conditional inference; max depth 3; min 3 distinct SKUs per child
trace.permutation_scheme: product tags: whole SKU district vectors within equal-support strata; district tags: districts within each SKU; y and v paired; max across all candidates
trace.sku_covariance: district demand weights; conditional variances independent; shared leaf posterior covariance
trace.unit_definition: SKU × district; complete observed and issued rows; at least one eligible day in each window
trace.winsorisation: per store/SKU 99th percentile across eligible 70-day history before aggregation
trace.overdispersion: sample variance of seven-day (A-E)/sqrt(E) baseline residuals, floored at 1
trace.forecast_error_variance: Per SKU/district, sample variance of eligible baseline seven-day log((A+0.5)/(E+0.5)) current-model residuals minus mean 1/(E+0.5) count-sampling variance, clipped at zero; log-rate units squared. Add this weekly systematic variance times (7/recent eligible days + 1/baseline eligible weeks) to each unit log-change variance. Uses historical issued weather and baseline outcomes only; part of the baseline may be in the current model training period. No percentage floor.
trace.drilldown_effect: Inverse-variance weighted mean unit log change transformed with expm1 × 100 at each actual tree prefix, before leaf and SKU shrinkage. Daily requests are raw eligible observations; siblings are within the same parent.

method.order_impact_scope: SKU order differences allocated by each leaf district forecast share; case total rounded. Disjoint district leaves do not duplicate total value.
method.value_method: Normal expected shortage difference under the adjusted demand distribution

cards.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.
cards.pallet_change_basis: Footprint of the change in total purchased cases; not a change in simultaneous warehouse peak occupancy.
cards.peak_capacity_scope: Whole warehouse with ALL cohort adjustments and current overrides already included together.

leaf.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.

trace.tree: inverse-variance conditional inference; max depth 3; min 3 distinct SKUs per child
trace.permutation_scheme: product tags: whole SKU district vectors within equal-support strata; district tags: districts within each SKU; y and v paired; max across all candidates
trace.sku_covariance: district demand weights; conditional variances independent; shared leaf posterior covariance
trace.unit_definition: SKU × district; complete observed and issued rows; at least one eligible day in each window
trace.winsorisation: per store/SKU 99th percentile across eligible 70-day history before aggregation
trace.overdispersion: sample variance of seven-day (A-E)/sqrt(E) baseline residuals, floored at 1
trace.forecast_error_variance: Per SKU/district, sample variance of eligible baseline seven-day log((A+0.5)/(E+0.5)) current-model residuals minus mean 1/(E+0.5) count-sampling variance, clipped at zero; log-rate units squared. Add this weekly systematic variance times (7/recent eligible days + 1/baseline eligible weeks) to each unit log-change variance. Uses historical issued weather and baseline outcomes only; part of the baseline may be in the current model training period. No percentage floor.
trace.drilldown_effect: Inverse-variance weighted mean unit log change transformed with expm1 × 100 at each actual tree prefix, before leaf and SKU shrinkage. Daily requests are raw eligible observations; siblings are within the same parent.

method.order_impact_scope: SKU order differences allocated by each leaf district forecast share; case total rounded. Disjoint district leaves do not duplicate total value.
method.value_method: Normal expected shortage difference under the adjusted demand distribution

notes.baseline: Simple rule: order up to 28-day average demand x (lead time + review days) x 1.25.
notes.lead_time: New orders arrive after the supplier's mean lead time; orders placed late in the week may land after the played period.
notes.autopilot: After the first week, Scoop refits cohort effects and places future orders automatically.
